parts.label: i
parts.ask: Show that \(k^2 - 4k + 5\) is positive for all real values of \(k\).

steps.why: \((k-2)^2 = k^2 - 4k + 4\), so take the 4 back off.

parts.answerText: Since \((k-2)^2 \geq 0\), \((k-2)^2 + 1 \geq 1 > 0\), so \(k^2 - 4k + 5\) is positive for all real \(k\).

parts.label: ii
parts.ask: Complete a student's proof by contradiction that there are no positive integers \(x\) and \(y\) with \((3x + 2y)(2x - 5y) = 28\). The student has shown that \(3x + 2y = 14\), \(2x - 5y = 2\) gives \(x = \tfrac{74}{19}\), \(y = \tfrac{22}{19}\), not integers.

steps.text: If \(x\) and \(y\) are positive integers, \(3x + 2y\) and \(2x - 5y\) are an integer factor pair of 28.
\(3x + 2y \geq 3 + 2 = 5\), so both factors are positive and \(3x + 2y\) is 7, 14 or 28.
steps.why: Say why the other factor pairs are impossible.

steps.text: With the student's case, \(3x + 2y = 14\), all three cases give non-integer \(x\) and \(y\).

parts.answerText: This contradicts the assumption, so there are no positive integers \(x\) and \(y\) with \((3x + 2y)(2x - 5y) = 28\).

check.answers: proof by contradiction: the assert searches positive integers up to 200 for a counterexample, and re-solves the three factor pairs with 3x + 2y >= 5
check.assert: not any((3*x + 2*y)*(2*x - 5*y) == 28 for x in range(1, 201) for y in range(1, 201)) and all(not (s[x].is_integer and s[y].is_integer) for s in [solve([Eq(3*x + 2*y, p), Eq(2*x - 5*y, 28 // p)], [x, y]) for p in (7, 14, 28)])
